title: Bitcoin Faucet Payout Index — August 2026
summary: Editioned snapshot of documented Bitcoin faucet and micro-wallet payout rails. Figures are taken from public official pages fetched on 2026-08-26. Typical claim amounts and sats/hour rates that require a logged-in dashboard or a timed trial are left unverified.

whatWasChecked: Official public pages and help centers for the live GetFreeBit faucet-desk partners (FaucetPay, Cointiply, RewardJoy/CoinPayU, Fire Faucet, FaucetCrypto).
FaucetPay withdrawal fee and minimum table at faucetpay.io/fees.
Cointiply Labs help articles on coin value, Daily Free Coins, cashout minimums, and fees.
Fire Faucet FAQ (firefaucet.win/faq) covering the 30-minute faucet, Auto Faucet/Fuel, and withdrawal rules.
FaucetCrypto Mintlify knowledge base on coins, faucet claims, country availability, and withdrawal minimums/fees.
HTTP reachability of freebitco.in (historical hourly BTC faucet listed on the desk but not a live partner).
how: Fetched public HTML/help pages on 2026-08-26 (UTC) with a standard browser user-agent. No accounts were created. No dashboards that require login were used.

Recorded only figures that appear on those pages. Converted BTC amounts to satoshis with the exact ratio 1 BTC = 100,000,000 sats. Did not convert USD-pegged platform coins to sats (that depends on the live BTC price at payout).
Partner/affiliate hrefs are resolved from site.config.ts or the existing faucet-referrals catalog. Official URLs in this file are untracked homepages.
notMeasured: No 30-day or even 24-hour earning trial was run. Average earning rate (sats/hour or sats/day) is unverified for every row.
Typical per-claim satoshi amounts that only appear after login (captcha rolls, ACP conversion, FaucetCrypto “Get Reward” coins) are unverified.
Exact Fire Faucet BTC network minimums (the FAQ says hover the battery icon on the logged-in withdrawal page).
Exact FaucetCrypto BTC coin floor (docs say BTC requires “a little bit more” than 1,000 Coins).
RewardJoy/CoinPayU cashout numbers: public pages returned an ad-blocker interstitial to this checker, so numeric fields are unverified.
Lightning Network payouts: not listed on FaucetPay’s public fee table; not claimed elsewhere without a source.
limitations: This is a documentation snapshot, not a live APY or income forecast. Offerwalls, PTC, and games can dominate faucet-claim math.
FaucetPay is a custodial micro-wallet and faucet directory, not itself a timed BTC faucet. It is in the table because it is the cashout rail most of the desk routes through.
Platform “Coins” are USD-pegged internal units. They are not satoshis.
Status “online” means the public site responded with documentation, not that a withdrawal succeeded today.
Skip clones and sites with no public terms. This edition does not add unaudited “best faucet” directories.

faqs.question: What does this index measure?
faqs.answer: It records publicly documented Bitcoin faucet and micro-wallet payout rules: typical claim size when published, claim interval, withdrawal minimum, method, fees, and operational status. It is a citable snapshot for August 2026, not a ranking of “best faucets.”

faqs.question: Did GetFreeBit measure sats per hour?
faqs.answer: No. This edition did not run a timed earning trial. Average earning rate is unverified for every row. If a later edition publishes sats/hour, it will state the exact window, account level, and whether offerwalls were included.

faqs.question: Why are some cells marked unverified?
faqs.answer: A field is unverified when the official page does not publish a number, the figure is behind login, or the public site blocked the fetch (for example RewardJoy’s ad-blocker interstitial). Unverified is preferred over an invented satoshi figure.

faqs.question: How should other sites cite this dataset?
faqs.answer: Cite the edition and check date, not a generic “GetFreeBit faucets” URL. Example: GetFreeBit, “Bitcoin Faucet Payout Index — August 2026” (checked 2026-08-26), https://www.getfreebit.com/indexes/bitcoin-faucet-payout/. Machine-readable copies are at the JSON and CSV download links on that page.

withdrawalMethod.notes: Lightning is not listed on the public per-coin fee table.

fees.value: On-chain normal 0.00001000 BTC (1,000 sats); priority 0.00005000 BTC (5,000 sats); Direct Transfer free. Fees marked dynamic with network congestion.
fees.notes: Help article “Why are Bitcoin fees so large?” explains UTXO/dust deposits; last updated 2021-12-21 on faq.faucetpay.io.

frequency.notes: Not a claim-interval faucet. Third-party faucets that pay into FaucetPay set their own timers.

averageEarningRate.notes: No timed trial. Homepage marketing figures (claims paid, users online) are not an earning rate.

usUsers.value: No US geo-block stated on the public home or fees pages checked.
usUsers.notes: Absence of a published country list is not an eligibility guarantee. Custodial wallet — enable 2FA; sweep to self-custody.

pairsWithFaucetPay.notes: This row is the FaucetPay rail.

rows.notes: Treat FaucetPay as a batching layer. On-chain BTC cashout from this rail is expensive relative to faucet dust; the fees page lists cheaper exits on LTC, DOGE, and others.
rows.risks: Custodial. Direct Transfer never hits the chain. On-chain BTC minimum (0.0012 BTC) is far above typical faucet drips.

payout.notes: Help docs describe Daily Free Coins as a captcha + Roll on Earn paths. The coin amount per roll is not published on the public help pages checked.

minimumWithdrawal.notes: Sats received at cashout depend on BTC’s price. Coins are USD-pegged, not satoshis. Confirmed on Labs help: What are Coins?; Common Withdrawal Questions.

withdrawalMethod.value: On-chain to BTC, LTC, DOGE, or DASH wallet via Cashout
withdrawalMethod.notes: Public help describes Cashout to a personal wallet. FaucetPay is not listed on the withdrawal articles checked.

frequency.notes: Daily Streak requires earning at least 300 Coins in a day and claiming the streak reward (help: How Does the Cointiply Daily Streak Work?).

usUsers.value: No country-block list found on the Labs help articles checked.

pairsWithFaucetPay.notes: Current public cashout docs describe direct crypto to your wallet. They do not document a FaucetPay option. Older third-party reviews may be stale.

rows.notes: Internal Coins: 10,000 = $1 USD (Labs help). Bitcoin cashout floor is 50,000 Coins. Terms can hold withdrawals for review; help also notes 5% annual interest on balances over 35,000 Coins when enabled.
rows.risks: Offerwall reversals. Custodial balance until cashout. Verification can be required on a withdrawal (30-day window or coins return to balance).

payout.notes: FAQ documents a 30-minute faucet and an Auto Faucet that converts ACP into chosen cryptos. Per-claim BTC sats and ACP-per-claim are not published on the public FAQ.

minimumWithdrawal.display: Varies by coin and network; FAQ range about $2.50–$25. Exact BTC sats only on the logged-in withdrawal page (battery icon per network).
minimumWithdrawal.notes: Range is official. Exact BTC mainnet vs other-network floors were not visible without login, so sats are unverified.

withdrawalMethod.value: On-chain to a wallet on the networks listed per coin (FAQ examples: Mainnet, BSC, Polygon); gift cards also mentioned
withdrawalMethod.notes: The 2026-08-26 FAQ does not mention FaucetPay. Older reviews that list FaucetPay minimums were not used.

fees.value: Withdrawals: platform covers network and processing fees. Instant Conversion of ACP: 5% fee. Crypto-to-crypto exchange on the Wallet page: free.
fees.notes: Daily withdrawal pace: $10/day default, $25/day Prime. A coin whose minimum exceeds the daily cap can still be withdrawn in full.

frequency.value: 30-minute faucet claim; Auto Faucet burns 1 Fuel per minute while running; daily bonus and Daily Tasks also documented
frequency.notes: Base Fuel recharges with level. First withdrawals may take 48–72 hours; later batches around 00:00 UTC.

averageEarningRate.notes: Auto Faucet USD value is described as independent of which crypto you pick; ACP cost per cycle varies. No sats/hour published. Weekend Happy Hour: +50% Auto Faucet for one hour at 02:00 and 14:00 UTC Saturday and Sunday.

usUsers.value: FAQ: open to users across the world. VPNs/proxies temporarily block earning pages.
usUsers.notes: World-open is not a US-specific legal review. Gift-card catalogs can still vary by country.

pairsWithFaucetPay.notes: Not listed on the current public FAQ. Do not assume a FaucetPay rail from older write-ups.

rows.notes: Balances are stored as USD value (FAQ). Completing offerwalls still depends on third-party providers. v5 Auto Faucet runs on Fire Faucet servers, not a browser miner (FAQ).

fees.value: 50 Coins for most assets; BTC, TRX, Polygon, BSC, and ETC “could be higher… but not much.” Deducted from the withdrawn amount.
fees.notes: Batch payouts: requests sit in a pool (Processing) then broadcast (Completed). If the pool threshold is not met, auto-broadcast after 24 hours (how-long article).

frequency.notes: Third-party reviews quote 25–40 minute timers. Those numbers were not on the official KB fetched 2026-08-26, so frequency stays unverified.

averageEarningRate.notes: Official answer: earnings depend on time, location, and tasks; “no fixed limits.” Not a sats/hour series.

usUsers.value: Available worldwide except China, Cuba, Iran, and Venezuela. Some offers still geo-restrict.
